basis: Motor peripheral neuropathy; muscle atrophy in 4/5 reflects denervation rather than direct muscle disease. Cardiomyopathy in 1/5 is below threshold.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle wasting in 4/5 is secondary to motor nerve damage; no independent muscle or skeletal pathology is established.

basis: Progeroid skin, skeletal changes and lipodystrophy define the syndrome; arterial stenosis and valve calcification annotated 80-99%. Retinal pigmentation alone does not establish ocular damage.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: generalized lipodystrophy and marked metabolic dysfunction are core features; the axis does not depend solely on separately diagnosed diabetes.

basis: Autoimmune subepidermal blistering disease; oral mucosal blistering and erosions occur in approximately one third, near the threshold.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: oral mucosal blistering and erosions affect approximately 30-35%, providing direct mucosal injury near the threshold.

basis: Retinal dystrophy, obesity/hypogonadism and digit anomalies define BBS4; renal abnormalities are major BBS criteria. Intellectual disability in 1/3 omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.renal: involved: structural renal abnormalities are major BBS diagnostic criteria and are documented in BBS4, despite unspecified frequency here.
decisions.neurologic: none under cap: intellectual disability in 1/3 qualifies, but retinal, endocrine, skeletal and potentially severe renal disease take priority.

basis: TGM5-related acral epidermal peeling is a skin disorder. Frequent hypermetropia annotation does not establish disease-caused ocular injury; allergy is separate.

decisions.ocular: none: despite the 30-79% annotation, hypermetropia is not an established direct manifestation of TGM5-related acral peeling skin syndrome.

basis: Trichomonas infection predominantly affects genital mucosa, outside the anatomical axes. Urinary disease occurs in subtypes and is not established across most patients.

decisions.renal: none: the definition describes vaginitis; urinary ancestry and a cystitis subtype do not establish urinary involvement across this umbrella concept.

basis: Oxidative phosphorylation defect with defining cardiomyopathy 9/9 and anemia 7/7; liver dysfunction 5/9. Hearing impairment in 1/1 omitted under cap and limited sampling.

decisions.haematologic: primary: intrinsic anemia in 7/7 is a defining hematologic feature of this mitochondrial disorder.
decisions.cardiovascular: primary: severe early cardiomyopathy in 9/9 is a defining manifestation of this oxidative phosphorylation deficiency subtype.

basis: Intellectual disability, seizures and psoriasiform dermatitis define the syndrome, each annotated 30-79%; an immune mechanism is not established by psoriasiform morphology.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: the evidence establishes psoriasiform dermatitis, which does not by itself establish psoriasis or an immune-mediated syndrome.

basis: Vascular and skin telangiectases plus recurrent nasal bleeding define HHT; GI lesions 60% with melena 30% support GI injury. Hepatic AVMs alone do not establish liver dysfunction.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: recurrent spontaneous nasal bleeding, present in 10/10, is a major diagnostic criterion; nasal mucosa belongs to the pulmonary axis.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic persistent skin telangiectases, present in 8/10, are defining vascular skin lesions and a major diagnostic criterion.

basis: Defining cutis laxa 4/4, emphysema 3/3 and bladder diverticula 3/3; GI malformations include pyloric stenosis 2/4. Joint hypermobility 4/4 omitted under cap.

decisions.renal: primary: urinary anomalies are defining; bladder diverticula occur in 3/3 and hydronephrosis in 2/4.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: pyloric stenosis occurs in 2/4; the three-primary cap prioritizes the more consistently affected skin, lung and urinary organs.
